newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's long-term PHIBOR rates down.
newsitem.headline: Manila's long-term PHIBOR rates down.

text.p: Long-term Philippine interbank offered rates (PHIBOR) slipped marginally as some banks anticipated a slight drop in Treasury bill rates on Monday, traders said.
The PHIBOR market will be closed on Friday for a holiday for All Saints Day, when Filipinos visit cemeteries to pay homage to the dead.
"Some banks expected the rates to go down since the Bureau of Treasury had cut down the size of its weekly offering," one trader said.
But another trader said the decline would not be significant as banks would opt to stay out of the market due to a new ambiguous administrative procedure set by the Treasury.

Officials were not immediately available to confirm the new rule but traders said the Bureau of Treasury had asked banks to open separate accounts with the Central Bank for each client doing secondary transactions.
The Treasury's aim might be to ensure a system by which they could track each deal for tax purposes, traders said.
Other rates remained unchanged. PHIBOR are average rates of foreign exchange forward quotes of banks.
